title: Maintaining Commitment Through Adjustment
opening: A failed method can be worth changing while the reason for the work still matters. Separate the purpose, outcome, repeatable process and specific method so you can see which commitment the evidence calls into question.

labels.comparison: Which level does the evidence challenge?
labels.comparisonIntro: Suppose a tutoring format produces completed sessions, but independent use of the material has not been checked. Keeping the same format is not proof of commitment to learning. First examine the result and the reason for the format.
labels.adherenceText: Helping someone use what they learn is a purpose; an outcome says what result would serve it. An outcome can change while the value remains, and a value or direction may also deserve reconsideration.
labels.valueText: Regular attempts and feedback form a repeatable process. If that process fails to produce the intended result, examine it rather than treating repetition as sufficient proof.
labels.outcomeText: A format, tool or exercise is a method serving the process. Changing it can preserve the goal. If evidence challenges the goal itself, a clever change of method will not settle that question.
labels.signalQuestion: Explore a part of the explanation
labels.rhythmTitle: Change the level the findings point to
labels.rhythmText: Name the value or direction, outcome, process and method. Locate what the observations challenge, then change that level while keeping the others visible or explicitly revisiting them. A higher purpose is not protected from inquiry. Revising an internal goal also does not cancel another person’s actual agreement; discuss any change that affects it.
labels.practice: Keep the commitments and proposed change visible
labels.practiceIntro: Use the parts of this note that help explain what changed and why. It is possible to retain a purpose, revise an outcome or reconsider the direction itself.
labels.private: This private note is optional. The six course questions remain separate.

labels.sourceQuote:
Maintaining Commitment Through Adjustment
Keep the different levels of commitment visible: the value or life direction, the
outcome, the repeatable process and the specific method. Changing the method can
preserve the goal. Changing a goal can preserve what made it matter. Examine the
level where the evidence points.

fields.label: The value or life direction at stake
The outcome intended to serve it
What to change, retain or revisit, including actual agreements

example.qualities: Suppose I want to help beginners use a skill independently.
example.contribution: The intended result is that they can use the skill in a new situation.
example.avoid: They make attempts and receive feedback.
example.present: The current method is the same tutoring exercise each week.
example.connection: Sessions are completed, but independent use has not been checked. That leaves the result unknown.
example.change: Choose an appropriate way to check independent use before deciding whether to change the exercise or the wider arrangement. Keep any real agreements visible.
